evidence.positive: Injected Mayo SIU^S14 messages into the running app at localhost:62333 via POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send with X-Tenant-Id: mayo-mayo (admin session login). Each message was a copy of the repo's real captured Epic fixture mayo-client-integration/src/test/resources/hl7/rormc-siu-s14-before.hl7 with a unique SCH-2 case id, a fake PMRN (99xxxxxx), and ZCS-5 populated with the exact strings from the ticket. All ACKed MSA|AA. Resulting rows in mayo-mayo.operations: case 990001 ZCS-5='3-Severe Systemic Disease' -> asa_status=ASA_3; 990002 '2-Mild Systemic Disease' -> ASA_2; 990003 '5-Moribund' -> ASA_5; 990007 legacy Roman 'III' -> ASA_3. The same values come back over the API: GET /api/admin/patients/by-pmrn/99000201/operations returned [{"caseId":"990201","asaStatus":"ASA_3","classification":"URGENT"}] and pmrn 99000203 returned asaStatus ASA_5. Upsert behaviour also exercised on resend: 990001 re-sent with '4-Severe Threat' moved ASA_3 -> ASA_4; 990004 re-sent with '2-Mild Systemic Disease' filled null -> ASA_2; 990002 re-sent with a ZCS carrying no ASA kept its existing ASA_2 (the non-null guard in DefaultHL7ProcessingContext).
evidence.negative: Same injection path, same fixture, ASA absent or unmappable. Case 990004 with the fixture's real ZCS form 'ZCS|BEFORE|N|ORSCH_S14' (no ZCS-5), case 990006 with an explicitly empty ZCS-5, and case 990005 with 'ZCS|AFTER|N|ORSCH_S14||9-Made Up' all persisted asa_status = NULL (psql on mayo-mayo.operations showed empty asa_status for 990004, 990005, 990006). The messages were provably not dropped: the same rows carry classification=URGENT and operating_room_name='RM OR 49 ROEI 01 303' from the same SIU, and GET .../by-pmrn/99000202/operations returned {"caseId":"990202","asaStatus":null,"classification":"URGENT"}. The unmappable value surfaced rather than vanishing: app log line 'WARN ... MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessor : Unmapped SIU ASA physical status ZCS-5=\'9-Made Up\' - hl7MessageId=01a0359a-48bd-71c8-9663-be2b63357e47'. Values '9-Made Up' and no-ZCS-5 produced no ASA, i.e. junk is not coerced into a status.
evidence.red_check: Pre-fix class swap. Took the shipped HEAD source of MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessor, removed exactly the OR-2678 additions (the AsaStatus import, the 'AsaStatus asaStatus = resolveAsaStatus(...)' line, the '.asaStatus(asaStatus)' builder call, and the resolveAsaStatus method), expanded @Slf4j/@RequiredArgsConstructor by hand since lombok is not on the runtime classpath, and added a distinctive boot marker log. Compiled it inside the app container with javac against $(cat /app/jib-classpath-file) and dropped the .class into /app/classes/com/guided/orci/integration/mayo/hl7/, which precedes /app/libs/mayo-client-integration-0.1.94-SNAPSHOT.jar on the classpath (position 2 vs 33), so the jar was never modified. Restarted the container; boot log confirmed the swap loaded: 'PREFIX-ASA-SWAP-ACTIVE processor build with no ZCS-5 parsing loaded'. Re-injected the same positive messages: cases 990101 ('3-Severe Systemic Disease'), 990102 ('2-Mild Systemic Disease') and 990103 ('III') all persisted asa_status = NULL while classification=URGENT still persisted, and 990104 ('9-Made Up') produced zero 'Unmapped SIU ASA' warnings. So the positive assertion and the warn-log assertion both went red. Reverted by deleting /app/classes/com/guided/orci/integration/mayo (only the mayo subdir I created; the pre-existing Result.class files were untouched) and restarting. Restore confirmed three ways: the mayo jar sha256 is unchanged at 9bc36b5dd509fbd2f59d930337afe66e149884a75db3850bc46fa73bbc9a0455, the PREFIX-ASA-SWAP-ACTIVE marker is absent from the post-revert boot, and a re-run of the positive case produced 990201 -> ASA_3, 990203 -> ASA_5, 990202 (no ZCS-5) -> NULL.

red_check_signature: PREFIX-ASA-SWAP-ACTIVE processor build with no ZCS-5 parsing loaded
caveats: Injection used the admin send endpoint (processMessageForAdmin -> processTenantMessage), which is the same code path as the live integration endpoint apart from apiTokenId; the real Epic-facing /api/integration/hl7 route was not exercised.

No captured Epic SIU in the repo actually carries a populated ZCS-5 - every fixture on disk has 'ZCS|BEFORE|N|ORSCH_S14'. The field position was taken from the ticket's sample text, so if Epic puts ASA in a different ZCS component than ZCS-5-1 in the live feed this validation would not catch it.
Numeric-prefixed forms exercised end-to-end were 2, 3, 4 and 5, plus legacy Roman 'III'. ASA_1 and ASA_6 are covered only by the existing unit tests, not by an injected message.

The red check swapped only the SIU processor class; the AsaStatus enum, the operations.asa_status column and the merge line in DefaultHL7ProcessingContext stayed in place, so it isolates the ZCS-5 extraction rather than the whole changeset.

Downstream consumers of asaStatus that landed in later commits (ProcedureRiskService pancreatectomy risk, the admin ASA edit endpoint and the Debug Operation tab) were not exercised beyond confirming OperationDTO serialises the field.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage is already solid and was written with the fix: AsaStatusTest covers numeric-prefixed, bare-number, Roman-numeral, blank, out-of-range and int-overflow inputs; MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest covers ZCS-5 numeric, Roman, absent and unmapped through the processor; DefaultHL7ProcessingContextSchedulingFieldsTest covers the non-null merge on upsert. Nothing in the parsing or merge logic is uncovered, so no new tests are strictly needed. The only real gap is that every processor-level ASA test uses a hand-authored message rather than a real captured Epic SIU, and there is no qa-suite coverage of ASA at all (grep for 'asa' in qa-suite returns nothing) - low value to add given the field is not yet surfaced in the clinical UI.
proposed_tests: Add a captured-fixture variant of rormc-siu-s14-before.hl7 with ZCS-5 populated and assert the processor maps it, so the parsing test is anchored to a real Epic message shape rather than a hand-authored one.

Add a processor test asserting a resend with no ZCS-5 does not clear an already-set asaStatus, locking the first-in-wins-on-null merge behaviour at the SIU level rather than only in DefaultHL7ProcessingContextSchedulingFieldsTest.

jira_comment:
Validated against a throwaway local build of main (e7eeafd6c) with the mayo-mayo tenant enabled. Verdict: deploy-ready.

How it was validated:

- Positive: real captured Epic SIU^S14 fixture (rormc-siu-s14-before) re-sent with ZCS-5 populated using the exact values from this ticket. 3-Severe Systemic Disease persisted asa_status ASA_3, 2-Mild Systemic Disease persisted ASA_2, 5-Moribund persisted ASA_5, and the legacy bare Roman numeral III persisted ASA_3. The same values come back over the admin operations API. Resends also behaved: a new ASA overwrites, a missing ASA leaves the existing one alone.

- Negative: the same fixture with no ZCS-5, an empty ZCS-5, and an unmappable 9-Made Up all left asa_status null. The messages were provably not dropped, since classification and operating room from the same SIU still persisted, and the unmappable value logged an Unmapped SIU ASA physical status warning rather than being coerced into a status.

- Red check: the pre-fix version of the SIU processor was compiled and swapped into the running container ahead of the shipped jar on the classpath. With it loaded, the same valid ZCS-5 messages persisted a null asa_status and the unmapped warning never fired, so both assertions went red. The swap was then removed and the restore confirmed by unchanged jar checksum and a re-run of the positive case.

Automation: the existing unit tests already cover enum parsing, processor extraction and the upsert merge, so no new coverage is required. Two optional additions are proposed - anchoring the processor ASA test to a captured Epic fixture with ZCS-5 populated, and asserting at the SIU level that a resend without ASA does not clear an existing value.

One thing worth flagging: no captured Epic SIU in the repo carries a populated ZCS-5, so the field position came from this ticket's sample text. If the live feed puts ASA in a different ZCS component this validation would not have caught it.
